ownership.project_facts: referenced .uef node projects and system-owned contracts
ownership.language_facts: this grammar and fixed compiler semantics only

shared_type_contract: ../registry/registry.json#/core_types and the project type-conversion semantics: .uefs uses the same fixed-width scalars, units, arrays, nominal enums, records, and no-implicit-conversion rules; its narrower operator subset and precedence are specified in this registry, not copied from the .uef operator table.

productions.system_decl: 'system' IDENTIFIER '{' { node_decl | external_endpoint | record_decl | enum_decl | link_decl | protocol_decl | hybrid_system_decl | delivery_policy_decl } '}'
productions.link_decl: 'link' IDENTIFIER '{' 'from' '=' reference ';' 'to' '=' reference ';' ('contract' '=' IDENTIFIER ';' | 'protocol' '=' IDENTIFIER ';') { property_decl } '}'
productions.protocol_body: '{' { property_decl | framing_block | header_block | sequence_block | payload_block | checksum_block | message_decl | receiver_block | behavior_block | protocol_state_machine } '}'
productions.primary_expression: finite_literal | STRING | BOOLEAN | reference ['[' expression [':' expression] ']'] | vector_literal | matrix_literal | map_literal | select_expression | parenthesized_expression

semantics.enum_values: Enums have fixed-width integer storage. Omitted values increment from zero in source order; explicit values define stable wire or persistent ABI values. Values must fit and be unique.
semantics.expression_resolution: Expressions are data-only, finite, and side-effect-free. Names resolve to local declarations or imported .uefs contracts; and/or short-circuit with and binding more tightly than or. No user code executes.
semantics.expression_operators: The .uefs precedence is one bounded index or half-open slice, unary + - not, left-associative * /, left-associative + -, one non-chainable comparison, and, then or. and/or short-circuit left to right. There is no power, cast, function-call, or arbitrary invocation syntax in .uefs. map constructs a statically expected record; select requires a boolean condition and identical branch type/unit/shape.
semantics.type_checking: Resolve scalar and unit semantics through the shared UETD project-language core type contract; resolve records/enums through the local system or imported node contracts. References must resolve to declared local values, imported contract fields, or exact node endpoints permitted by the enclosing link. No implicit numeric, enum, unit, shape, or record conversion; no dynamic dimension, pointer, null, or runtime allocation. Every system expression is checked against its property or endpoint contract.
semantics.contract_import: A contract import resolves one normalized relative path beneath the declared system source root. It imports only named records, enums, protocol contracts, and endpoint facts; it cannot execute code, traverse outside the project root, or recursively compile sibling node projects.
semantics.protocol_mapping: Each message field maps to one logical record field unless marked protocol_internal; raw_payload=true is required for opaque messages. Message-field offsets are relative to that message payload, fragment offsets are relative to their fragment payload, and header/sequence offsets are absolute frame offsets. Offsets and widths are byte/bit precise, nonoverlapping, and in bounds; gaps require explicit reserved fields. Scaling means decoded_value=wire_integer*scale+offset and its inverse uses declared rounding and overflow. Signed encoding, byte/bit order, reserved bits, version, sequence, checksum range/placement, freshness, and incomplete-frame behavior are explicit; generated struct layout is never wire ABI.
semantics.hybrid_system: Bindings name local nodes, external endpoints, and links only. They do not define callable remote functions. Every endpoint direction and message must have a declared link owner, protocol, delivery/recovery policy, and local receiving contract. External FPGA implementation code is outside UETD generation.
semantics.multi_target_generation: Each node is independently type-checked and built for its exact target. Cross-node type compatibility is checked against the system contract. Partial build results identify the completed and failed nodes and do not imply a complete deployable system.
